text: At 18 months post-treatment the authors report improvements from baseline in the Moderate Cohort in mean±SE MDS-UPDRS Part III OFF scores (−18.8±6.6), describe possible clinical benefit, and state that a phase 2 randomized controlled study is planned to confirm these findings. (low confidence)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: REGENERATE-PD (NCT06285643) is registered as a phase 2 randomized, double-blind, sham surgery-controlled study of intraputaminal AAV2-GDNF in adults with moderate stage Parkinson's disease. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: The registry record for the CAP-003 phase 1/2 trial of intravenous gene therapy in Parkinson's disease with a GBA1 mutation (NCT07011771) shows the status WITHDRAWN with an enrollment count of 0, and gives as the reason that a per protocol stopping rule was met for a separate trial for a different disease state and different experimental therapy that utilized a similar technology. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-22)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: In the phase 2 randomised trial of bilateral AAV2-GAD delivery in the subthalamic nucleus in advanced Parkinson's disease, the primary outcome measure was the 6-month change from baseline in double-blind assessment of off-medication UPDRS motor scores. (low confidence)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: In a double-blind trial of AAV2-neurturin delivered to the putamen and substantia nigra in advanced Parkinson disease, the authors report no significant difference between groups in the primary endpoint (change from baseline: AAV2-neurturin, -7.0 ± 9.92; sham, -5.2 ± 10.01; p = 0.515) among Fifty-one patients, and conclude that it was not superior to sham surgery. (low confidence)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: A review article on clinical trials in GBA1-associated Parkinson's disease states that where GBA1 variants exert a toxic gain-of-function effect, gene therapy alone may not be sufficient, and that a strategy combining an antisense oligonucleotide with gene therapy to restore functional GBA1 may be required. (low confidence)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: The phase 1b trial NCT04167540 of AAV2-GDNF (AB-1005) enrolled 11 participants, 5 in the Mild Cohort and 6 in the Moderate Cohort, per the authors' abstract and the registry record. (medium confidence)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: The authors report that all participants experienced treatment-emergent AE, most of them transient and perioperative, and that serious AEs (n=5) were unrelated to AAV2-GDNF in this early-phase study. (low confidence)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: The registry record for REGENERATE-PD (NCT06285643) lists a primary outcome of change from baseline to Month 18 on PD Motor Diary (normalized Good ON time per Hauser Diary), an actual enrollment of 59, and the status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: The authors of the AAV2-GAD sham-surgery trial report that at the 6-month endpoint the UPDRS score decreased by 8·1 points in the AAV2-GAD group and by 4·7 points in the sham group, and that the AAV2-GAD group showed a significantly greater improvement over the 6-month course of the study (RMANOVA, p=0·04). (low confidence)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: In the AAV-hAADC study of bilateral intraputaminal infusion in patients with moderately advanced PD, with low-dose and high-dose cohorts of 5 patients in each, the authors report the gene therapy was well tolerated, but 1 symptomatic and 2 asymptomatic intracranial hemorrhages followed the operative procedure. (low confidence)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: A review describes the PROPEL study (NCT04127578) of AAV9-GBA1 (PR001/LY3884961) as a phase 1/2a study that aims to evaluate the safety and tolerability of PR001 in individuals with moderate to severe PD who carry at least one GBA1 mutation, with PR001 administered via intracisternal injection. (low confidence)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

text: The FDA announcement states that Kebilidi (eladocagene exuparvovec-tneq) is an adeno-associated virus vector-based gene therapy indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) deficiency, and that Kebilidi is the first FDA-approved gene therapy for treatment of AADC deficiency. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-11-14)
keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors
